Modals To Express Intention (Will, be going to, would, want to)
You use modals to express a willingness to do something or to talk about your plans and intentions for the future.

You use will, want to, be going to or would to talk about your plans or about something you mean to do in the future.
Example:
I'd like to eat as soon as possible.
I'm going to verify that with the kitchen.
I want Michael to get to the market right away.

You use will to express willingness about an action or situation.
Example: Will you go into the main fridge and check for me?
Sure. I'll do that right away.
Will you go into the main fridge to see how many there are?
I'm going to call Michael in. I want him to get to the market right away.
I'd like to eat as soon as possible.
The Perfect Infinitive After Modals for Suggestion
You use the Perfect Infinitive with modal verbs to talk about hypothetical situations and to suggest possibilities.
You use the Perfect Infinitive after modals like could, might, should, would to talk about suggestions, unreal situations, or possible outcomes.

Structure:
modal verb + have + past participle
You use the Perfect Infinitive with modals to suggest something that could have been done instead of something else.

Example:
You could have left the fridge door open to avoid this situation.
Michael must have counted them already.
They might have been eaten since last night.
I would have had mussels, but I guess the tuna tartare will be fine.
Will we have been served before noon?

images.text:
In the kitchen:

Vanessa: We've had a 10 orders of the fresh mussels, Rachel. Will you go into the main fridge to see how many there are?
Rachel: Michael must have counted them already. He left a note.
Vanessa: Great but I'd like you to double check. They might have been eaten since last night.
Rachel: If you insist!
Vanessa: Here, I'll get them out of the fridge. I need to know exactly how many there are.
Rachel: The fridge door must have been left open. It stinks! It smells putrid ... like rotten meat!
Vanessa: Oh my God! I'm going to call Michael in. I want him to get to the market right away.
Rachel: Right ... because Michael is so team-oriented!
Vanessa: Remember what I said about attitude, Rachel.

In the dining room:

Alexander: I'm afraid we are out of the “Moules du Jour”. I could recommend ...
Customer: That's outrageous! We ordered them ages ago and now you tell us there aren't any? Will we have been served before noon? My clients here are hungry. Can you please recommend something? I'd like to eat as soon as possible.
Alexander: The tuna tartare is divine ... or the veal scallopini.
Customer: I would have had mussels, but I guess the tuna tartare will be fine. Ten orders at this table and more pinot grigio please. How long will it be?
Alexander: Before I tell you, I'm going to verify that with the kitchen.

In the kitchen:

Alexander: Okay everyone, the customer on table five is going to have my head if we don't have enough tuna tartare!
Vanessa: Everything in the fridge must have gone off. I've called Michael and he's at the market. I'll text him now to get fresh tuna.
Alexander: Get them to chop it for us! Do you think having it on the table in ten minutes is feasible?
Vanessa: Oh my God! Rachel may have lost her marbles. She's taking her shoes and socks off in front of the customers!
Alexander: I've got to see this!
